proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the comparator record with the exact published sampling layer, the calendar-varying extension, and the proved rate limitation.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup, Assumptions 2.1--2.3, a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model, and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect. The present theorem works in exactly that layer upon taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and shows by a block construction that no uniformly faster rate follows from those conditions alone.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, a reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects, with covariance and pair-mass formulas, normalization, and exact rational diagnostics. The base i.i.d. superpopulation layer is not the published Arkhangelsky--Imbens--Lei--Luo class, and the two are incomparable. A separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer coincides with the published class upon taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\); there the tensor approximation has rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), homogeneous recovery is direct, and a block construction shows that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\) alone. A randomized three-period counterexample lies in a published-class subclass, so calendar-varying nonreduction transfers upward. For absorbing supports, graph connectivity gives the exact rank dimension and adjacent ratios give only a pointwise Cramer sign certificate; global sign-chamber enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and leaves its calendar-varying DATE equation beyond scope. Its class allows arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence. The base i.i.d. conditional-mean layer instead uses a common propensity conditional on pretreatment covariates, so it is not the published class and the two layers are incomparable. Existing event-study decompositions also do not provide the reshaped finite-memory calendar-by-lag tensor, an absorbing-support graph-rank law, or exact fixed-law sign certificates.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path forward loading tensor shared algebraically across two explicitly separated sampling layers, a rate-explicit anchor-faithful published-class theorem, and ordered diagnostics that use absorption only where it is mathematically necessary.
project_justification.fill: The project proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization and rational diagnostics, and a positive-law absorbing graph formula for kernel dimension. In a separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer that contains the published class exactly when the support is their \(\mathcal S^*\), it proves the calendar-varying tensor approximation at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), recovers the homogeneous theorem directly, and gives a block witness showing that the stated conditions imply no uniformly faster coefficient rate. A randomized three-period witness belongs to a published-class subclass and therefore transfers calendar-varying nonreduction to the larger published layer. The fixed-law adjacent-ratio result remains a pointwise Cramer certificate, not a global chamber classification.

sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\) and a positive ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\); absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries. In the separate published layer, taking \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S^*\) reproduces the published support exactly.
sampling_model.units: Population identification uses i.i.d. triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) from \(P\). This base superpopulation layer is not the published class and is incomparable with it. A separate theorem uses the published possibly dependent, non-identically distributed unit-indexed triangular array and its maximal-correlation condition, so homogeneous recovery is direct in that layer rather than transferred from the base class.
sampling_model.treatment: In the base algebra, \(W_i\) may be any path in the declared finite binary support. The published layer uses its arbitrary binary-path support \(\mathcal S^*\). Ordered adoption-time results explicitly restrict support to absorbing paths.
sampling_model.overlap: The population layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\). The published layer instead uses known unit-specific propensities \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_*\) on the reshaping support and defines its RIPW weight to be zero off that support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a correct common generalized path propensity and pathwise conditional means. The anchor-faithful statistical theorem is for the published known-propensity estimator and yields the \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\) coefficient approximation; it does not assert cross-fitted or doubly robust inference.

prose_updates.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence. The base i.i.d. conditional-mean class is not their published class and is incomparable with it. The separate unit-indexed theorem retains their class exactly upon taking the reshaping support to be \(\mathcal S^*\), retains the grand intercept in their equation \(4.2\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying finite-memory effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and directly recovers their Theorem \(4.1\) under homogeneity. Its block construction shows that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\) alone. The randomized three-period nonreduction witness lies in a subclass of the published calendar-varying layer, so the failure transfers upward. Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not study assignment-law reshaping of finite-memory lag regressors. Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment. De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) recover time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags in complex designs. Wright (2026) supplies adjacent public-manuscript evidence on conventional event-study diagnostics, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients; none supplies the present tensor and ordered support geometry.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved forward algebra covers arbitrary finite binary-path supports. Causal identification in the base superpopulation layer requires consistency, pathwise conditional mean random assignment, overlap, the stated calendar-memory conditional mean, and full rank; that layer is not the published class and is incomparable with it. The separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer contains the published class exactly upon taking the reshaping support to be \(\mathcal S^*\). Under its known propensities, grand intercept, and Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), the theorem proves the coefficient approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\) and shows that no uniformly faster rate follows from the stated conditions. The randomized three-period counterexample lies in a published-class subclass, so its failure of calendar-homogeneous reduction transfers to the larger calendar-varying published layer. Absorption is used only for the Green-kernel identity, graph-rank theorem, and adjacent-ratio certificate. The graph dimension formula requires every reshaping mass to be positive and is false at the simplex boundary without deleting zero-mass paths. The adjacent-ratio result is pointwise. No central limit theorem, asymptotic normality, global sign-chamber enumeration, inverse-image optimization, closest feasible loading, worst-case contamination optimization, or cross-fitted doubly robust result is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: In the separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer, the theorem proves the calendar-varying tensor approximation at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), directly recovers the published homogeneous conclusion, and supplies a block-dependent witness showing that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from the stated conditions.
statement_notes.gap: The published theorem leaves calendar-varying dynamic DATE analysis beyond scope, and Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\) alone do not yield a uniformly faster coefficient approximation rate.
statement_notes.consumer: Users can interpret the published weighted regression through the tensor under the exact published sampling layer, without an invalid inclusion argument from the incomparable base class and without reading the rate as a central limit or doubly robust claim.
